schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (TEMP.MIN_DATE + 1) = A.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT TEMP.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS FRACTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS MIN_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS TEMP JOIN ACTIVITY AS A ON TEMP.PLAYER_ID = A.PLAYER_ID
q2: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN TEMP.MINDATE+1=A.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(DISTINCT A.PLAYER_ID),2) AS FRACTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID,MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS MINDATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS TEMP JOIN ACTIVITY A ON A.PLAYER_ID = TEMP.PLAYER_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. The key difference lies in the denominator of the division. In Q1, the denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT TEMP.PLAYER_ID), which counts distinct player IDs from the subquery TEMP. In Q2, the denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT A.PLAYER_ID), which counts distinct player IDs from the joined ACTIVITY table. In most cases, these are the same, but when a player has multiple events on the same date, Q2 may count the same player multiple times in the denominator, while Q1 always counts distinct players once.
